summary: fix(store): one canonical resource name, snake-cased dispatch, loud default arms, parent_id on write-through rows, real sync_state.total_count
reason: The printed CLI spells the same resource two ways and normalises nowhere. The sync registry, the DDL, resourceIDFieldOverrides and loadCompanyResources use snake_case (journal_entries); the generated read/mutation commands, the UpsertBatch dispatch switch, the upsertSingleObject switch and resourceParentKeyColumns use kebab-case (journal-entries). Three consequences, all silent. (1) UpsertBatch's switch had NO default arm, so bank_accounts and journal_entries never matched an arm and their typed tables stayed empty on a fully synced file (issue #6 section 1: 0 rows against 63k generic rows). (2) resourceParentKeyColumns missed those two, so resourceStorageID returned a BARE id instead of id\0<companySlug> and two companies' journal entries with the same journalEntryId collided on the resources primary key -- data loss in the only table the detectors read. (3) The read/live path's writeThroughCache wrote rows under the kebab name AND without parent_id, so loadCompanyResources (which filters on $.parent_id) could not see one of them: two disjoint populations of the same resource. Separately, sync_state.total_count was a per-run running counter that was never reconciled against actual rows and drifted in both directions. The fix is a hand-authored CanonicalResource in internal/store/resource_name.go (kebab->snake, validated against the closed set derived from the DDL plus the generic names the generated call sites use; an unknown HYPHENATED name is an error, an unknown separator-free name stays an opaque generic type because `resources` is a generic mirror and the printed regression suite writes synthetic types through these entry points), called at every storage boundary: Store.Upsert, Store.UpsertBatch, resourceStorageID, upsertSingleObject, both resolve*WithStrategy entry points (which cover writeThroughCache and resolveLocal in one place) and writeMutationResponseToStore. The three hyphen maps and the four hyphen literals inside UpsertBankAccounts/UpsertJournalEntries are re-spelled snake. Both dispatch switches gain a default arm that errors when a canonical name owning a typed table reaches it. writeThroughCache takes the company slug parsed from the /companies/{slug}/... request path and stamps parent_id onto each item. sync persists store.CountResources instead of its running counter. sync gains --company so a run cannot walk every book in the mirror (only agensia is a Fiken testCompany). doctor cross-checks sync_state.total_count against the resources row count and the typed-table row count per resource and reports bare storage keys and orphaned kebab populations with the resync hint. No migration code: per owner decision the repair is `sync --full --company <slug> --resources journal_entries,bank_accounts`. Three literals in the generated internal/store/upsert_batch_test.go were re-spelled to match (two resource_type assertions, one hyphenated synthetic type). Follow-up: --full now also deletes the scoped company's existing rows for each named resource before the refetch (store.ClearCompanyResources, FTS kept in step), because resetting the cursor alone left the pre-fix bare-key rows alongside the correctly keyed ones and the company was counted twice by loadCompanyResources. Gated on an explicit --company plus an explicit --resources list, so an unscoped --full keeps the printed behaviour.

validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... pass. New hand-authored tests: internal/store/resource_name_test.go (kebab->snake for all five split names, rejection of unknown hyphenated and malformed names, idempotence, and parity between typedTableResources and the CREATE TABLE statements parsed out of store.go, plus canonicality of resourceParentKeyColumns and resourceIDFieldOverrides); internal/store/dispatch_test.go (UpsertBatch("journal_entries") now fills the typed table -- it filled 0 rows before this patch -- kebab and snake produce one identical population, two companies' entries with the same journalEntryId no longer collide, unknown names error and write nothing, and every typed resource has a live dispatch arm); internal/cli/mirror_canonical_test.go (slug parsing, parent_id stamping, real row count over the running counter, --company scoping, and a scan of every resource literal the generated commands pass to the mirror asserting the closed set covers it). Verified end to end against the Fiken test company agensia only: after `sync --full --company agensia --resources journal_entries,bank_accounts` the journal_entries typed table went 0 -> 100 rows, the agensia generic rows carry the id\0agensia storage key, and `doctor` reports no row-count disagreement for either resource. The --full clear was verified on agensia: journal_entries rows with parent_id agensia went 200 -> 100 and bare-key agensia rows 100 -> 0, with the typed table still at 100.
